CASH IN TRANSIT HEISTS 2018

By: Nicky Troll | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
A bomb goes off in the country every day. Armed gangs run the streets with AK47s in the suburbs. The target – cash-in-transit.

Unique Selling Point:
- topical issue
- great visuals
- sexy element hearing it from a robber first hand

Summary:
A wave of cash-in-transit heist are gripping the country. So far there have been 160 CIT robberies this year.

We’ve told the story before from security insider’s point of view. This time round we hear from CIT informant close to the network of robbers. We look at cash-in-transit heists and the battle for intelligence.

When it comes armed robberies the biggest bounties are in CIT trucks – millions of rands is transported on South Africa’s roads every day – hundreds of moving targets ready for criminals to hit.

We dig deeper and expose the driving forces behind this crime trend that appears to be mutating and spreading like a virus.


Further information:
SUMMARY

In 2014 there were 180 cash-in-transit incidents; in 2017, there were 370 — a staggering 105% increase in just three years. In 2018 it’s 152 for the first five months of the year.

The criminals are not amateurs – they are highly skilled and playing a game of militaristically planned robberies. New research & first hand accounts from an active cash-in-transit robber paints frightening picture of a highly sophisticated criminal underworld.
WHAT’s THE STATUS QUO?
Explosives are being used widely across SA to break into cash management systems like safes, ATMs and cash in transit vehicles. When we broke the story in 2015, there had been 8 in the space of 9 months – but it has become the MO of choice.
In 2015, we showed how criminals get explosives from officials in the SANDF. This time round we explain how commercial grade explosives are obtained and sold.
FOOTAGE
There is quite a bit of footage of criminals of cash-in-transit robberies taking place. I also have exclusive footage from inside the CIT trucks and filmed from the perspective of the truck. I also have the video of the CIT guard being executed in Newcastle in February. I also have footage of a guards being shot at – you can see the terror – it’s chilling.

THE GUARDS ARE SAYING ENOUGH
The Motor Transport Workers Union and FEDUSA have spoken out against the conditions and the fact that many of the CIT guards and drivers live in fear and feel that they are not adequately prepared or armed to face off with the level of robbers attacking CIT trucks.
I am trying to get a guard to speak to us – it would be hidden identity – they are not permitted to grant interviews openly.
THE INDUSTRY
We interview Wahl Baartman about the current crime trends, and what the industry is doing – Fidelity is the biggest company operating in SA. He admits that guard conditions could be improved.
WHY ARE THE ROBBERS NOT BEHIND BARS?
The problem is that these robbers get arrested, but they get released on bail – despite the evidence, despite having previous related cases against them. We highlight these issues with actual examples.
SAPS have launched a joint project with private security to get to grips with the scourge.
THE MUTHI MIND GAME
Muthi playes a massive role in CIT scene – sangomas are a crutial part of the prep before robbers do a job – we explore this element by interviewing Dr Thobane from UNISA who has done her thesis on the criminal career of armed robbers with reference to CIT robberies – she did a whole section the role of sangomas and muthi.

Press Release:



Cash-In-Transit
A new wave of cash-in-transit heists is gripping the country and armed syndicates carrying AK47s in the suburbs, are running the streets. Fed-up security guards are protesting, demanding government intervention, but with 159 CIT robberies already this year, specialised law enforcement agencies seem helpless to put an end to the violent heists. Carte Blanche investigates why these criminal organisations have become so brazen.


Script:


STRUCTURE – CIT 2018

VO: In 2015, we first exposed the use of black market explosives in cash in transit heists.

UPSOUND OLD SCRIPT:
INFORMANT: And how much for the Safe stuff?
SUPPLIER: for the safe it’s R3500.

VO: We showed how an informant bought four cartridges of watergel explosives – enough for at least four robberies. Three years later, using explosives is the standard operating procedure for cash-in-transit robbers - it’s become, a warzone.

LINK: Brazen gangs armed with automatic weapons and explosives lawlessly run the streets The target…….. millions of rands in cash being transported, on our roads, around our cities every single day. Bringing the attack on the cash security industry right to your door step.

INFORMANT: //there will be more.// Even Bheki Cele will never stops this…

VO: It’s a high risk, high profit crime – and gangs are not going to back down – it’s just too lucrative says a paid industry informant who moves in CIT Heist circles – he cooperates with the authorities and security companies.

INFORMANT: // when it comes to cash in transit it’s much better – you can get R300 000, // R400 000, even R800 000, even a meter, you can get one million.
DEVI: What’s the most amount of money you have ever made in a single hit?
INFORMANT: it was R1.2 million.

VO: The financial losses in stolen money, has trebled since last year – with robbers making off with hundreds of millions of rands.

With a 40 % spike in CIT robberies since 2016 - the hits are becoming more violent with massive bounties at stake. Criminalogist Dr. Mahlogonolo Thobane has done extensive research on CIT robberies having interviewed 40 convicts.

DR THOBANE: When security becomes tighter, the harder your target becomes, the more force and violence they have to use.

VO: So far two civilians have been killed in shootouts . Police Minister Bheki Cele believes this is a crime against the state.

MINISTER: This crime has pitched up on the cash heists which is nothing but terrorism – it puts // a lot of fear on South Africans




VO: Cash-in-transit guards are the first in the line of fire - this year, guard injuries are up by 82% with 62 wounded and five guards killed so far.

Watch as these robbers go after CIT crews. KEEP MUSIC…..SPACE….

This week cash in transit crews took to the streets demanding government regulations for combat training, improved armoured vehicles and more firepower.

In the meantime, crews around the country are feeling the pressure every single day. Michael Burke has faced off with criminals for 20 years.

DEVI: When you leave home in the morning how do you feel?
MICHAEL: worried, worried, you never know when is the day that you won’t return… the last time when you greet your wife in the morning…. (teary)
DEVI: but that’s hectic…
MICHAEL: it is yah.

LINK: The risk is real – every day you you get into a CIT vehicle, you could get shot or even killed. The reality is these are 2 to 3 man crews taking on gun wielding gangs of up to 15 men – they out manned, out gunned.

VO: Besides being out-numbered, the design of these vehicles also make it difficult to fight back considering the small space and limited shooting ports. Michael, says the danger only hits home when you’re caught in the crossfire.

MICHAEL: // at first you think you are going to die, and then you just start fighting back and try not to die (nervous laugh) and protect the assets.

VO: And the robbers know what’s at play - they have between 5 and 8 minutes on the scene of a heist and will get the job done whether the security cooperate or not.

INFORMANT: Time is money, I have to move.
DEVI: If someone is going to become difficult what are you going to do /
INFORMANT: we are going to shoot that person // if I don’t shoot that person I am going to be in shit, definitely.

VO: Wahl Bartmann from Fidelity Security says the industry fully appreciates that they’re up against professional criminals and that these attacks are not random.

WAHL: If we look at the amount of shots are fired // to shoot on a moving target and your grouping is so professional and all in a ten centimetre. It looks like they’ve got either military training or some specialised training to act and to react in certain circumstances.

VO: And that theory is on the mark says the informant – they are experienced in specific skills.

INFORMANT: // some of us they are from exile, some of us ex-policemen, former MK, and other former hitmens. // Each and every person got his job, you got the best drivers, the best shooters and the men putting the explosives.

LINK: While cash security companies invests millions of rands in technology and intelligence, criminals are as committed to their jobs.

VO: They evolve and adapt the way they operate, finding ways to circumvent the cash security industry’s defences.

WAHL: The cost that we incur and the preventative measures that we put in place – additional back up vehicles, helicopters, all of that really puts our industry under huge pressure and I don’t know if all the companies will survives this.

VO: The financial losses to security companies are huge – so far this year, R64-million has been lost just as a result of 49 damaged CIT vehicles.

WAHL: this is really having a big impact not only on the companies but on the economy as a whole.

VO: As a largely unbanked population there is a huge demand for cash, there are around 2500 cash in transit vehicles on the road every day – each one a potential target for robbers.

LINK: It’s become a uniquely South African crime trend. The driving forces are an economy where cash is still king for the majority of people and a criminal underworld that operates with military precision and insider intelligence.

DEVI: are security company insiders involved?
INFORMANT: Some of the cars, even those who are working at control room, they know this car has got this money.
DEVI: and you pay for information?
INFORMANT: Yes, there’s no lion’s share – if we are each getting one million, one million, it means that person must get one million. // INT1 M36

VO: But the industry is not convinced that security insiders are the norm.

WAHL: We’ve had vehicles that have been bombed that had no cash on them // we do everything possible to minimise internal involvement - but we cannot exclude it, unfortunately it happens. INT1 M31

VO: There is a whole network of players involved in each heist – the industry informant confirmed that the explosives are sourced from mines and the getaway cars are usually stolen – everything they need, can be bought at a price.

DEVI: Where do you get the weapons from?
INFORMANT: we buy weapons, I can get the R4 from these guys from SANDF, we get the guns from SAPS, we get the guns from Mozambique, we get the guns from Natal.
DR THOBANE: Police can be involved in three ways, the police can drive a getaway vehicle, called an off-ramp, to protect the loot and the weapons, and then secondly the police can be bribed to make the docket disappear or the police can be involved in diverting response.

VO: Dr. Thobane’s says besides police involvement, crime displacement, the recent release of CIT convicts and weak crime intelligence have allowed robbers to believe that they are above the law.

DR THOBANE: We’ve had problems in the crime intelligence and then offenders saw it as an opportunity to hit because they basically could say a could of steps ahead of our police, so they felt untouchable because we don’t have much of a crime intelligence.

LINK: Only a fraction of the CIT robbers get caught by the authorities, and even then they more often than not they don’t end up behind bars, but rather back on the street out on bail.

VO: NPA Spokesperson Luvuyo Mfaku denies this.

LUVUYO: I do not know where this notion that they get released on bail, it is not supported by any empirical evidence.

VO: But the informant says he is evidence enough.

DEVI: Have you ever been arrested?
INFORMANT: Yah, lot of times.
DeVI: For cash in transit?
INFORMANT: yes
DEVI: What you doing here then?
INFORMANT: Money makes the world go round… // we pop up lot of money – we are paying councillors, councillors are paying the prosecutor.
DEVI: Did it ever get to court?
INFORMANT: Yes, I go to court, but they are going to throw it.
DEVI: Why do they throw it out?
INFORMANT: lack of evidence
DEVI: you are laughing when you say lack of evidence – why?
INFORMANT: We are paying money

VO: Claims Dr. Thobane’s research supports– criminals manage to avoid incarceration all the time.

DR THOBANE: Anybody working in the criminal justice system that is willing to take money, a kickback, they can bribe that person.

DEVI: What if we allow it to continue?
MINISTER: Let me make a very clear statement – we are not going to allow it to continue. You need to put all your brains together, but not only your skills from the SA police, but also from the industry work together from the cash – cit industry.

VO: With joint operations launched, the NPA says they’ve also changed their modus operandi for dealing with CIT cases – they have now assigned their top prosecutors and bail must be opposed.

DEVI: But it does mean that something wasn’t working before…
LUVUYO: in respect of these sophisticated and high profile cases we are saying lets get our best from the onset to take this matter forward so that we do not have a situation where we say we might have slipped somewhere. INT2 M7

VO: But even if convictions are secured, Dr. Thobane says there is a slim chance of rehabilitation.

DR THOBANE: based on the research that I have conducted the cash in transit robbers said that they can never ever be rehabilitated. // they said it’s the only life that they know, the minute that they get out of prison they continue on committing robberies.

VO: The industry informant confirmed Dr. Thobane’s research.

INFORMANT: that’s the life I chose – no one force me into it, and to maintain my standard I have to go on.

VO: The Minister says this lawlessness has to be stopped.

MINISTER: as the police we will have to broaden our kind of working with a full understanding that cash heist is a culmination, it is the epitome of the fear factor kind of crime. The time is up – I have made it very clear // that we are ready to go toe to toe.

 
PROMOS
PROMO 1
VO: Cash in transit gangs have the country’s cash security industry under siege.

MICHAEL: At first you think you are going to die, and then you just start fighting back and try not to die

PROMO 2
VO: A wave of cash-in-transit heists are gripping the country and it seems armed gangs are running the streets

MINISTER: This crime has pitched up on the cash heists which is nothing but terrorism

VO: We expose the driving forces behind this crime trend.

PROMO 3
VO: It’s like a warzone. Armed gangs run the streets with AK47s, setting off explosives in the suburbs. The target – cash-in-transit.

INFORMANT: There will be more. Even Bheki Cele will never stops this – I’m telling you.

PROMO 4
VO: Armed gangs run the streets with AK47s, setting off explosives in the suburbs. The target – cash-in-transit.

MINISTER: It is the epitome of the fear factor kind of crime.

VO: It’s a high risk, high profit crime and gangs are not going to back down.

INFORMANT: There will be more.// Even Bheki Cele will never stops this //

VO: With 2500 CIT vehicles on the road every day – the bounties are big.

INFORMANT: you can get R300 000, // R400 000, even R800 000, even a meter, you can get one million. INT1 M6

MINISTER: Let me make a very clear statement – we are not going to allow it to continue. You need to put all your brains together, but not only your skills from the SA police, but also from the industry work together from the cash – cit industry. metadata.Summary: A wave of cash-in-transit heist are gripping the country. So far there have been 160 CIT robberies this year. We’ve told the story before from security insider’s point of view. This time round we hear from CIT informant close to the network of robbers. We look at cash-in-transit heists and the battle for intelligence. When it comes armed robberies the biggest bounties are in CIT trucks – millions of rands is transported on South Africa’s roads every day – hundreds of moving targets ready for criminals to hit. We dig deeper and expose the driving forces behind this crime trend that appears to be mutating and spreading like a virus.
metadata.Further information: SUMMARY In 2014 there were 180 cash-in-transit incidents; in 2017, there were 370 — a staggering 105% increase in just three years. In 2018 it’s 152 for the first five months of the year. The criminals are not amateurs – they are highly skilled and playing a game of militaristically planned robberies. New research & first hand accounts from an active cash-in-transit robber paints frightening picture of a highly sophisticated criminal underworld. WHAT’s THE STATUS QUO? Explosives are being used widely across SA to break into cash management systems like safes, ATMs and cash in transit vehicles. When we broke the story in 2015, there had been 8 in the space of 9 months – but it has become the MO of choice. In 2015, we showed how criminals get explosives from officials in the SANDF. This time round we explain how commercial grade explosives are obtained and sold. FOOTAGE There is quite a bit of footage of criminals of cash-in-transit robberies taking place. I also have exclusive footage from inside the CIT trucks and filmed from the perspective of the truck. I also have the video of the CIT guard being executed in Newcastle in February. I also have footage of a guards being shot at – you can see the terror – it’s chilling. THE GUARDS ARE SAYING ENOUGH The Motor Transport Workers Union and FEDUSA have spoken out against the conditions and the fact that many of the CIT guards and drivers live in fear and feel that they are not adequately prepared or armed to face off with the level of robbers attacking CIT trucks. I am trying to get a guard to speak to us – it would be hidden identity – they are not permitted to grant interviews openly. THE INDUSTRY We interview Wahl Baartman about the current crime trends, and what the industry is doing – Fidelity is the biggest company operating in SA. He admits that guard conditions could be improved. WHY ARE THE ROBBERS NOT BEHIND BARS? The problem is that these robbers get arrested, but they get released on bail – despite the evidence, despite having previous related cases against them. We highlight these issues with actual examples. SAPS have launched a joint project with private security to get to grips with the scourge. THE MUTHI MIND GAME Muthi playes a massive role in CIT scene – sangomas are a crutial part of the prep before robbers do a job – we explore this element by interviewing Dr Thobane from UNISA who has done her thesis on the criminal career of armed robbers with reference to CIT robberies – she did a whole section the role of sangomas and muthi.
